clue.text: Length I needed in soil when my adversary won?

indicators.note: needed in tells us the length and the I must be placed inside the word for soil

parts.note: dust is dry soil or dirt
an ell is an old measure of length, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a longer reach would have saved them when their opponent beat them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a sword fight lost for want of reach, but 'Length' is the old cloth measure. 'when ... won?' is surface colour: an opponent who could win is one who duels with you.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a duel are each other's opponents, so my adversary is the other combatant.

clue.text: Sediment is piled up in store

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the word for store

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: piled up, in a down clue, means the word is is read upwards

explanation.surface: Silt has been heaped up in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' turns IS into SI, which goes into DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a layer of matter that settles out, like silt from a river.

clue.text: As part of village's plan, 'a delightful open space

indicators.note: As part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A village planning document promises a pleasant open area.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open level area, often a seafront promenade.

clue.text: In France, nothing much is written about port

indicators.note: is written about means the word for much goes round the French word

parts.note: a lot means much
rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: In France, hardly anything gets written about a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorient is a seaport in Brittany, north-west France.

clue.text: After second disagreement Her Majesty is more formal

indicators.note: After says the royal letters come after the second and the disagreement

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: After a brief quarrel, the Queen becomes stiffer in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are starchy and stiff means formal, so stiffer is more formal.

clue.text: Container affected by material for cheese-making

parts.note: a case is a box or container
to be in something, as in pain or in love, is to be affected by it

explanation.surface: A tub has been tainted by what goes into making cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Casein is the main protein in milk, the substance that curdles to form cheese.

clue.text: Place with many ears that hear not

definitions.text: Place with many ears that hear not

parts.words: Place with many ears that hear not
parts.note: ears here are the heads of grain on cereal stalks, which cannot hear anything

explanation.definitionFit: A field of wheat or corn holds countless ears of grain.

clue.text: Obsequious type makes glib speech about a new leader

indicators.note: about means the word for glib speech goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a spiel is a slick patter

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of new

explanation.surface: A fawning person gives a smooth talk about a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIEL goes round A and N (new's leader).
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniel is used of a fawning, servile person, from the dog's devoted manner.

clue.text: It looks like I've begun painting by numbers with this technique

definitions.text: It looks like I've begun painting by numbers with this technique

parts.words: It looks like I've begun painting by numbers with this technique
parts.note: split as ... the name looks like a claim to have counted beyond zero, as in starting to paint by numbers

explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting method where paint is laid on thickly so brushstrokes stand out.

clue.text: Exam row about George I — a threatening but ineffectual man

parts.note: an exam paper is the set of questions sat in an examination

indicators.note: about means the word for row goes round the letter for George

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
G is a standard abbreviation for the name George

explanation.surface: A test on the reign of the first Hanoverian king, George I, who was all bark and no bite.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' after George adds nothing to the wordplay; it only makes the king George I, the first Hanoverian, for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger is an idiom for a person or power that looks fearsome but has no real strength.

clue.text: Are they always poisonous first and last?

definitions.text: Are they always poisonous first and last?

indicators.note: first and last asks for the opening and closing letters of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A doubtful question about whether certain snakes are venomous through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first and last letters of 'always' (A, S) and of 'poisonous' (P, S). The whole clue also asks about snakes that are, at least in part, poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, Cleopatra's legendary choice of serpent.

clue.text: Circumstances, say, with regard to romantic relationships

parts.note: to state something is to say it
of can mean concerning, as in 'speak of it'
affairs are love affairs, romantic liaisons

explanation.surface: A situation that describes someone's love life.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of affairs is an idiom for the current situation or set of conditions.

clue.text: Vehicle finds trail curtailed by pile of rocks

indicators.note: curtailed means the word for trail loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: a track is a trail or path
a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A farm vehicle's path is blocked by a heap of boulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the last letter from TRACK to leave TRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a powerful farm vehicle for pulling machinery.

clue.text: Close inside and open outside during hours of darkness

indicators.note: inside places the word for close within the word for open
outside says the word for open goes round the other

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
nigh means close or near

explanation.surface: Something shuts indoors and opens outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight means through the night, while it is dark.

clue.text: Give him the first bit of baggage and he'll possibly work

definitions.text: Give him the first bit of baggage and he'll possibly work

indicators.note: the first bit of means only the opening letter of baggage is used
possibly signals that the letters of he'll may be rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Hand a hotel porter your first bag and he might get going.
explanation.walkthrough: B starts baggage; 'possibly' rearranges HE'LL into ELLH; OP (opus) means work. The whole clue also describes a porter who works once given a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellhop is a hotel porter who carries guests' luggage to their rooms.

clue.text: Moscow's leader surrounded by tradition in famous Russian building

indicators.note: surrounded by means the letter goes inside the word for tradition

parts.note: heritage is tradition handed down

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of Moscow

explanation.surface: A Moscow chief is steeped in tradition at a celebrated Russian landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is a great museum in the old Winter Palace.

clue.text: German city with 500 residents it's displaced

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: displaced means the letters of it's are moved out of the word residents

explanation.surface: A German city where five hundred inhabitants have been forced from their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' is not an anagram signal here: the letters of it's are lifted out in order, leaving the rest unshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital of Saxony in eastern Germany.

clue.text: Author said to be more correct

indicators.note: said means the word for author is heard, not seen

parts.note: a writer is an author

explanation.surface: Some writer claims to be more accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Righter is the comparative of right, meaning correct.

clue.text: Weak transmitter taking in mid- Wales

indicators.note: taking in means the word for transmitter holds the letter within

parts.note: a sender transmits signals

indicators.note: mid- points to the middle letter of Wales

explanation.surface: A low-powered radio mast picks up central Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of WALES is L, which goes inside SENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight or weak, as in slender chances.

clue.text: Officer looked up to, one man finally ousting another

indicators.note: finally ousting means one name replaces the other at the end of the word

parts.note: to be admired is to be looked up to
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward
Al is a man's name, short for Albert

explanation.surface: An officer was respected, until one man eventually pushed another out.
explanation.walkthrough: Both men are short names, Al and Ed, a crossword staple; 'finally' fixes the swap at the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a naval officer of the highest rank.

clue.text: Apart, to be sure, and split up

indicators.note: split up means the letters of sure and and are broken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Separated, certainly, and broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means into separate pieces, as in torn asunder.

clue.text: What animals with a stomach up on top could be?

definitions.text: What animals with a stomach up on top could be?

indicators.note: on top says the turned stomach sits above the animals in the down answer
up, in a down clue, means the word for stomach is read upwards

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach
ants are small animals

explanation.surface: A question about what creatures with an inverted belly would be.
explanation.walkthrough: TUM read upwards gives MUT, placed above ANTS. The whole clue also describes freakish animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutants are creatures changed by genetic mutation, often freakishly.

clue.text: Most juicy novel with gripping sin

indicators.note: gripping means the word for sin holds the novel inside

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: The steamiest book has a sin at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush means rich and succulent, so the lushest is the juiciest.

clue.text: Genuine transom undone, by chain in N. America

indicators.note: undone means the letters of the two words are taken apart and put together differently

explanation.surface: A real crossbeam over a door has come apart, next to a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'undone' rearranges GENUINE TRANSOM; 'by' only joins wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Mountains are a range in Vermont, part of the Appalachians.

clue.text: A number of horses bolt

explanation.surface: A herd of horses runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a stock of horses kept for breeding; a stud is also a bolt or rivet with a head.

clue.text: American channel is very successful, a number admitted

parts.note: golden means very successful, as in a golden period
the gate is the number of spectators let into a sports ground

explanation.surface: A US television channel is a big hit, with many viewers let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' is British for the attendance at a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Gate is the strait joining San Francisco Bay to the Pacific.

clue.text: An animal hugs its companion endlessly — having landed up here?

indicators.note: hugs means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a rat is an animal; the article gives the leading A

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the companion is dropped

parts.note: animals boarded the Ark in pairs, so a rat's companion is another rat

explanation.surface: Two animals on the Ark cling together until it comes to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAT holds RA (RAT without its end). Noah's Ark is said to have landed on Ararat, so the companion is the rat's partner on the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Noah's Ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat after the Flood.

clue.text: In favour of gamble, taking ultimately short view

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a spec is a speculation, a gamble

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of short

explanation.surface: Someone backs a bet while taking a short-term outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view or outlook over a landscape.
